summary: Shared REST Hyper runtime adapter now binds stateless messenger, mail, social, and community write routes from JSON bodies into existing typed REST dispatchers.
claim_boundary: This slice proves local adapter-edge JSON binding for stateless write routes over the existing bounded Hyper body collector and service-owned typed REST dispatchers. It does not claim stateful community vote/moderation binding, database persistence, broker publishing, live Oyatie Cloud tenant workload deployment, Gateway/TLS/DNS rollout, ArgoCD sync, branch-protection state, or remote CI green.

best_practice_research.source_quality: official docs.rs API documentation for serde_json 1.0.150
best_practice_research.used_for: Confirmed serde_json::from_slice deserializes JSON bytes and fails when the input shape does not match expectations, supporting fail-closed adapter-edge parsing.

best_practice_research.source_quality: official docs.rs API documentation for serde_json Value
best_practice_research.used_for: Confirmed Value represents valid JSON objects/arrays/scalars and exposes object/string/array accessors used for explicit adapter DTO mapping without adding serde derives to domain/API crates.
Grounded use of the Idempotency-Key header at the HTTP write boundary and fail-closed missing-key behavior.

source_basis.use: Runtime route classification, JSON body/header binding, response shaping, direct dispatch tests, and TCP loopback tests.
Messenger service-owned typed write dispatcher and REST request/receipt types.
Mail service-owned typed write dispatcher and REST request/receipt types.
Social service-owned typed write dispatcher and REST request/receipt types.
Community create-post typed dispatcher and stateful vote/moderation route distinction.

findings: JSON parsing stays in the shared runtime adapter instead of leaking serde_json into API/domain/usecase crates.
The adapter calls existing service-owned typed dispatchers rather than duplicating business logic.
Four stateless write routes now execute over local Hyper TCP, making the services more tenant-workload-ready for the future Oyatie Cloud substrate.
The adapter still separates local proof from live cloud deployment, Gateway, TLS, ArgoCD, and persistence claims.
Missing/invalid JSON or headers fail closed with 400 instead of silently defaulting.
Path/body identifier drift is rejected before typed handler execution.
HTTP header lookup is case-insensitive, matching HTTP semantics while preserving fail-closed required-header behavior.
JSON error responses escape control characters so hostile request values cannot break response JSON shape.
Stateful community vote/moderation routes remain honest 501 seams instead of fabricating missing backing state.
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: HTTP 400 with error_code path_body_drift when channel_id body value conflicts with the routed channel_id path capture.

findings: Service launchers can now send real JSON over the existing Hyper listener for the four stateless write paths using one common header contract.
Route catalog counts now distinguish probe, contract-only, JSON-write, and stateful typed-write-plan routes.
Local TCP loopback coverage asserts receipt event types for all four stateless write routes.
Regression tests cover path/body drift rejection, case-insensitive headers, and JSON control-character escaping.

alternatives_named: Add serde derives to all API structs
Keep all write routes at 501 until a full cloud deployment exists
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Use serde_json::Value only at the adapter edge to parse bounded JSON bytes, map explicitly into existing framework-free request structs, and avoid serde leakage into lower layers.
rejected_reasons: Serde derives on API/domain structs would widen dependency surface.
Hand-rolled JSON parsing would be more error-prone and less standard.
Keeping stateless write routes at 501 would preserve an avoidable runtime integration gap.

findings: No secrets, credentials, tenant data stores, or external endpoints were added.
The JSON parser runs after the existing Hyper adapter body cap, preserving bounded body collection.
Required Idempotency-Key and policy/request headers fail closed when missing.
F7_security.owasp_class_review: API input validation and mass-assignment avoidance through explicit field mapping

findings: Per-request work is one bounded JSON parse plus explicit field extraction for small write DTOs; no DB/broker/network calls are introduced.
Header lookup prefers exact map hits and only falls back to a small case-insensitive scan across request headers.
Policy-decision, audit-correlation, idempotency, and scope headers remain explicit request inputs and are echoed only as receipt metadata.
Idempotency-Key handling accepts HTTP case variants and aliases while preserving fail-closed missing-header behavior.
Reverting removes one adapter-edge dependency allowance and JSON-binding code without changing service-owned API/usecase/domain behavior.
Responses include low-cardinality runtime_handler, service, method, path, and event_type fields suitable for future loopback smoke probes without claiming production telemetry.
Existing probe and contract-only behavior remains source-compatible; stateful routes preserve 501 rather than changing semantics prematurely.
Slice id and runtime_handler names describe the exact adapter-edge JSON binding scope.
tasks/plan.md and tasks/todo.md now record the stateless JSON binding and remaining non-claims.
serde_json is isolated in the shared REST runtime adapter; lower layers remain serde_json-free.
The shared runtime adapter remains a composition adapter over REST crates and the canonical Hyper adapter, preserving framework and business-logic boundaries.
serde_json was already a workspace dependency; registry/dependency-rationales.json now explicitly allows this adapter crate for runtime-edge JSON body binding.
Field extraction is explicit per route and rejects missing/invalid fields; it does not mass-assign arbitrary JSON into domain structs.
The existing backbone package matrices already include the shared REST runtime adapter from the prior slice; focused checks cover the new JSON binding behavior.
